For the Petitioner : Mr. Suraj Kumar, Advocate For the Respondents : Mr. J. F. Toppo, G.A. - V ---------
06/20.03.2023 Heard Mr. Suraj Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. J. F. Toppo,
learned G.A. - V.

In this writ application, the petitioner has prayed for a direction upon the respondents to pay the final pension amount, gratuity as well as other legitimate dues along with the interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
The petitioner was appointed on the post of Assistant Teacher on 14.06.1986 and had superannuated from the service on 29.02.2020.

During his service period the petitioner was made an accused in a case under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code for which the petitioner remained under suspension, vide Memo No. 2355 dated 16.09.2019 and it was revoked by the respondent no.
3 on 26.12.2009.

It has been submitted that the petitioner has been paid some retiral dues and he has been granted provisional pension but the gratuity has been withheld apart from certain other dues which has led to a financial crisis being faced by the petitioner.

sentences.text: Mr. J. F. Toppo, learned G.A. - V submits that the pension rules have been amended and in case of a legal proceeding till its conclusion the delinquent employee shall be given provisional pension and the gratuity shall also be withheld.
It has been submitted that in view of the amendment the petitioner cannot claim any further relief save and except what has been admitted by the Department.
The petitioner seems to have been paid most of the retiral dues and he is primarily aggrieved with the fact that he is being paid provisional pension and the gratuity has also been withheld.

However,
in view of the amendment which has been relied upon by the learned G.A. - V, the same seems to have been adhered to and since a criminal case is pending against the petitioner, no interference is necessitated with respect to non-payment of the full pension as well as gratuity amount as the same shall be dependent on the outcome of the judicial proceedings.
In view of the above, therefore, this writ application stands disposed of.

(Rongon Mukhopadhyay, J.) Umesh/-
